newsitem.title: UK: Musical "Tommy" rises from grave for awards.
newsitem.headline: Musical "Tommy" rises from grave for awards.

text.p: 'Tommy', the rock musical about the deaf, dumb and blind kid who played a mean pinball, has risen from the grave to scoop three top theatre awards.

The musical, based on a 1969 rock opera record by The Who, folded this month after less than a year in London's West End despite some rave reviews. It picked up three trophies at Sunday's Olivier Theatre awards -- best musical, director and lighting.
Rock star Pete Townshend now plans to take "Tommy" on a 50-week tour of British provincial theatres but admits it could not compete with London's big budget musicals.
Impresario Cameron Macintosh was rewarded for the 500,000 pound ($810,800) revamp of the troubled "Martin Guerre" when the freshly relaunched show won the Best New Musical award.
Anthony Sher won the best actor award for his part in "Stanley" at the National Theatre. Janet McTeer was picked as best actress for her role in "A Doll's House."
